title: Exam 2 annotated public pathology lecture photos
status: images pending upload to public repository
note: All photographs originate from the user's uploaded annotated lecture PDFs and are not included in this text manifest. The public game activates a photo when its matching JPG exists.

images.caption: Polyp versus papilloma
images.studyPrompt: Identify surface shape, stalk, and papillary projections. Gross pattern is not enough to establish invasiveness.

images.caption: SCC keratinization
images.studyPrompt: Find keratin pearls and nests of squamous tumor cells; determine whether the basement membrane is breached.

images.caption: Papilloma vs invasive SCC
images.studyPrompt: Compare intact basement membrane on the left with tumor nests infiltrating dermis on the right.

images.caption: Smooth muscle tumor contrast
images.studyPrompt: Compare orderly smooth muscle bundles with atypia and infiltrating irregular spindle growth.

images.caption: Hemangiosarcoma microarchitecture
images.studyPrompt: Look for malignant endothelial cells making irregular blood-filled channels and wrapping around collagen.

images.caption: Soft tissue sarcoma grade
images.studyPrompt: Grade 1 versus grade 3: compare cell differentiation, nuclear atypia, mitoses and invasion.

images.caption: Plasmacytoma hof
images.studyPrompt: Identify eccentric nuclei and perinuclear pale area typical of plasma cells.

images.caption: Amyloid with plasma-cell tumor
images.studyPrompt: Spot extracellular pink amyloid deposits and distinguish them from collagen or necrosis.

images.caption: Low-grade mast cell tumor
images.studyPrompt: Find differentiated mast cells, eosinophils and collagen, with relatively mild atypia.

images.caption: High-grade mast cell tumor
images.studyPrompt: Find anisokaryosis, mitoses, collagenolysis and architecture distortion; compare with low grade.

images.caption: Histiocytic sarcoma
images.studyPrompt: Find marked anisocytosis/anisokaryosis and multinucleated giant cells in malignant histiocytic tumor.

images.caption: Rosette vs pseudorosette
images.studyPrompt: True rosette has a central lumen; pseudorosette lacks one and often surrounds a vessel or fibrillary region.

images.caption: Insulinoma with IHC
images.studyPrompt: Compare H&E nests to synaptophysin and insulin staining; use clinicopathology to establish functionality.

images.caption: Biopsy choice
images.studyPrompt: Incisional biopsy samples representative lesion and interface; excisional biopsy allows margin assessment.

images.caption: Hypercalcemia of malignancy
images.studyPrompt: PTHrP-mediated humoral hypercalcemia: compare AGASACA and lymphoma examples; do not infer bone metastasis.

images.caption: Hypertrophic osteopathy
images.studyPrompt: Look for smooth periosteal proliferation along long bones and connect it to thoracic mass.
